clue.text: Celebration meal provided by Pygmalion's beloved

parts.note: a gala is a festive celebration or special occasion
tea is a light afternoon or evening meal in Britain

explanation.surface: A festive dinner laid on by the sculptor's sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth Pygmalion carved a statue and fell for it; in later retellings the statue, brought to life, is given this name.
explanation.definitionFit: The ivory statue Pygmalion loved, animated by Aphrodite, is traditionally named so in post-classical versions of the myth.

clue.text: Looks for key weapons

parts.note: G is a musical key
lances are long spears used by mounted knights

explanation.surface: Someone searching for a set of keys and some arms.
explanation.definitionFit: Quick looks are brief glimpses at something; the plural noun fits the plural definition.

clue.text: Wycliffite uplifted everyone in the name of christ

indicators.note: the letters for everyone go inside the title for Christ

parts.note: Lord is a name given to Christ

indicators.note: in a down clue, being lifted up means the word for everyone is read from bottom to top

parts.note: all means everyone

explanation.surface: A medieval reformer raises the whole congregation in Christ's name.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'uplifted' signals reading upwards; 'the name of christ' is a title of address, not a personal name, which is the trap.
explanation.definitionFit: Followers of the fourteenth-century reformer John Wycliffe were known by this name.

clue.text: Dance, Oliver

definitions.meaning: a lively 1960s dance done by rotating the hips
Oliver ... is the orphan hero of the Dickens novel

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the hip-swivelling 1960s craze; the other is the surname of Dickens's workhouse orphan who asked for more.

clue.text: South-American tangerine production

indicators.note: a production of these letters means making something new out of them

explanation.surface: A citrus fruit grown on a South American farm.
explanation.definitionFit: Something from the country of Buenos Aires is described with this adjective, a synonym of Argentinian.

clue.text: Barren trees uprooted around one lake

indicators.note: the rearranged trees are placed around the pieces for one and lake
trees torn up are thrown into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
L is the standard abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: A bleak landscape where trees have been torn up around a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uprooted' rearranges TREES into STERE, and 'around' wraps that round IL.
explanation.definitionFit: Barren land is infertile, unable to produce crops or offspring.

clue.text: Consequently the cover is secure

parts.note: so means therefore or consequently
a lid is a cover for a pot or box

explanation.surface: Since the lid is on, the container is safe.
explanation.definitionFit: Something firm and dependable is secure in the sense of being stable and sound.

clue.text: Place peas close by pieces of veal

indicators.note: to place letters is to set them in a new arrangement, here the words peas and close

explanation.surface: A cook putting peas beside slices of veal on the plate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Place' looks like part of the instructions to a cook but is the anagram signal; PEAS and CLOSE together rearrange into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: These are thin boneless slices of meat, typically veal, beaten flat and fried.

clue.text: To deduce that the answer is negative is hell

parts.note: to infer is to deduce from evidence
no is a negative reply

explanation.surface: Concluding that the reply is a refusal feels like torment.
explanation.definitionFit: Dante's poem gave Italian's word for hell to English as a name for the underworld.

clue.text: Lad more disposed to exhibit a noble dignity

indicators.note: disposed means arranged or set out differently, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A boy more inclined to show off an aristocratic bearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposed' looks like 'inclined' but rearranges LAD and MORE.
explanation.definitionFit: Dignity here means a rank or title; this is the rank held by a count's British equivalent.

clue.text: A trainee telling tales about joining a union

parts.note: L stands for learner, as on a learner driver's plate
telling tales means telling lies

explanation.surface: A trainee spinning yarns concerning signing up to a trade union.
explanation.walkthrough: L-plates mark a learner driver in Britain, hence L for a trainee.
explanation.definitionFit: To ally is to unite or combine, so forming an alliance is joining in a union.

clue.text: A cigarette-lighter? The devil it is!.

definitions.meaning: an old name for a friction match used to light a pipe or cigarette
the name of Satan before his fall

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are the same name: the fallen angel Satan, and the Victorian brand of match for lighting a smoke.

clue.text: Totally innocent Australian outlaw gets punished

parts.note: chaste means pure and innocent
Ned Kelly was a famous Australian bushranger

explanation.surface: A bushranger who was completely innocent is nonetheless sentenced.
explanation.definitionFit: To be disciplined or corrected, especially into humility, is to be chastened.

clue.text: Inveigled into being guided around an ancient city

indicators.note: the word for guided goes around the ancient city

parts.note: led means guided
Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: Someone tricked into a guided tour of an old city.
explanation.definitionFit: To be enticed by trickery or temptation is to be drawn in like prey to bait.

clue.text: Grass the southern border

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for southern
an edge is a border

explanation.surface: Informing on the southern frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a grass-like plant growing in wet ground, so a type of grass in the broad sense.

clue.text: Spell-binding character in a French ante-room

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Spell-binding character in a French ante-room (9)': no parse of 'in a French ante-room' builds the answer (EN for 'in' leaves CHANTER unaccounted for); likely an OCR garble, and a search gave nothing.
annotationWithheld.clue: Spell-binding character in a French ante-room

clue.text: Where selected pupils are doing extremely well

definitions.meaning: the best pupils are placed in the highest class at school

explanation.definitionFit: Literally being in the highest class at school, and idiomatically being at one's best.

clue.text: Stop white ant spreading round North America

indicators.note: the insect stretches around the letters for North America

parts.note: white ant is another name for a termite

explanation.surface: Halting the advance of an insect pest across a continent.
explanation.definitionFit: To end something is to bring it to a stop.

clue.text: High spirits result in an resounding hurrah

definitions.meaning: a loud cheer of approval, a fine shout of hurrah

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means merriment, and read literally it is a fine shout of approval.

clue.text: Old offender upset one pope with a question of gravity

definitions.text: Old offender upset one pope with a question of gravity

parts.words: Old offender upset one pope with a question of gravity
parts.note: the astronomer tried by the Inquisition angered Pope Urban VIII by questioning orthodoxy, and studied falling bodies

explanation.surface: A historical rebel who scandalised a pope over a serious matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gravity' reads as seriousness, but it is the physics of falling objects he investigated.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pisan scientist was condemned by the Church for heliocentrism and pioneered the study of gravity.

clue.text: Circuitously rode round a little

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go round the word for a little
travelling by a roundabout path suggests the letters of rode are scrambled

parts.note: a bit means a little

explanation.surface: Someone took a roundabout ride around a short distance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Circuitously' signals an anagram of rode while the whole clue also describes the answer, a roundabout journey round a small object.
explanation.definitionFit: To have travelled in a circle around something is to have circled it, as by a roundabout ride.

clue.text: Tasty juice I had concentrated

parts.note: sap is the juice of a plant
I had compressed into a contraction gives I'd

explanation.surface: Delicious juice I'd drunk in concentrated form.
explanation.definitionFit: A rare word meaning having flavour, savoury or palatable.

clue.text: Alleged reason for the oral tradition?

definitions.meaning: a false excuse given to hide the real motive
spoken lore that comes before anything is written down

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a false excuse; read as two parts, it is what came before writing, as spoken lore did.

clue.text: She puts clothes on shelves in the kitchen

definitions.meaning: a theatre assistant who helps actors into costume
a sideboard with shelves for crockery

explanation.definitionFit: A theatre helper who clothes actors, and a kitchen sideboard with shelves for plates.

clue.text: The sign of a liberal painter

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, stands for a painter

explanation.surface: The mark of an artist of progressive views.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scales is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: Dog bit the end of the violin strings

definitions.text: the end of the violin strings

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow or tail them
a piece is a bit

explanation.surface: A dog chewed through the strings of a violin.
explanation.definitionFit: On a violin, the strings are anchored at the lower end to this wooden plate.

clue.text: Irascible instruction to examine a Cartesian coordinate

parts.note: to test is to examine
y is the vertical coordinate in the Cartesian system

explanation.surface: An irritable demand to check a point on a graph.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean short-tempered and easily irritated.

clue.text: Peel heartened by note from minister for the armed forces

indicators.note: the word for peel has its middle filled by the note

parts.note: to pare is to peel
D is a musical note

explanation.surface: Peel encouraged by a memo from a defence minister.
explanation.walkthrough: Peel looks like Sir Robert Peel, the prime minister, but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A military chaplain, a clergyman serving soldiers, is commonly called this.

clue.text: Stole it in error? That's an understatement

indicators.note: letters set down in error are misplaced, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Admitting one stole something by mistake is putting it mildly.
explanation.definitionFit: This figure of speech affirms by denying the opposite, as in 'not bad', a classic form of understatement.

clue.text: Where one lives, so to speak

definitions.meaning: to speak to an audience formally

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the location of a home; the other is to make a formal speech to listeners.

clue.text: He attends to the mess with obvious success!.

definitions.text: He attends to the mess with obvious success!

parts.words: He attends to the mess with obvious success
parts.note: a soldier or hospital attendant who cleans up, leaving things tidy afterwards

explanation.surface: A man cleaning up a mess and doing it well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mess' suggests untidiness and also an army mess; the attendant's title, read as an adjective, means tidy.
explanation.definitionFit: A military or hospital attendant bears this title, and as an adjective it means neat and well arranged.

clue.text: Eastern church reader who puts down his cross

parts.note: a lector reads lessons in church

explanation.surface: A reader from an Eastern church who lays down his crucifix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' suggests a crucifix but is the X a voter marks on a ballot paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A voter marks an X on the ballot paper to choose a candidate.
